title: Parker listened to Schoenberg and Bartok
summary: Parker's tastes and his parents' reaction to Pierrot Lunaire.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: You have a story I read about Charlie Parker, where you discovered that he listened to Charles Ives.

No, he listened to Schoenberg, “Pierrot Lunaire,” yeah, when I was a kid. I mean, with Bird’s and he listened to Bartok, he liked Bartkok and Schoenberg. So, I remember going to the library and getting um uh … Stravinsky was not quite so deep and Bartok was sort of in the pocket. But I think when my parents heard me listening “Pierrot Lunaire,” you know, the early 12 tone stuff, which is really “out” [makes weird noises to demonstrate], you know, [laughs] wild intervals. I think my parents were quite ready to accept my hanging out with the Stravinsky and Bartok. They said, “That’s okay, [laughs] the kid’s okay, but what is he listening to now?” [laughs] They must have had their doubts. “That’s not jazz, is it?”
